eligibility_reason: Imprint is an LLM-driven pipeline (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct throughout, per p. 5) that writes structured Interaction Records into an evolving memory M at run time as new observations arrive, via a three-stage online compression process — Event-Prototype Assignment, Interaction Importance filtering, and Interaction Consolidation (p. 2, p. 4 Fig. 2 caption) — and later retrieves top-k entries from that same self-written memory to condition each new question's answer (p. 4, Section 3.3, Eq. 3). This is a run-time write followed by cross-query retrieval over a store the system itself populates, not retrieval over a fixed corpus (E3 does not apply). No hardware/cache optimisation (E1), no parametric-only memory (E2), no secondary study (E4), memory is the entire contribution not incidental (E5), and the paper is well over four pages with full evaluation (E7 does not apply).

facets.justification: Memory entries are compared and merged via cosine similarity of contextual and action-object embeddings (event-prototype threshold δg = 0.75, consolidation threshold δm = 0.75, p. 4–p. 5), and retrieval ranks candidate entries with a weighted cosine-similarity score over object/action embeddings, Eq. 3 (p. 4). No separate structured schema, graph, or file store is described in the given pages.

The paper frames its write mechanism explicitly as 'online memory compression': incoming records are filtered by an importance score and then 'merged with similar observations into the compact memory M (Interaction Consolidation)' (p. 4, Fig. 2 caption); p. 2 describes the same process as producing 'compact long-term memories' as records arrive, reducing memory footprint 2.3× (p. 1).

Base retrieval ranks memory entries by a declared weighted-cosine top-k score, Eq. 3 (p. 4: sk = γ1 cos(eoq,eok) + γ2 cos(eaq,eak) + γ3 w(fk), TopK selected). For questions with temporal constraints, this ranked set is then explicitly filtered by a declared rule using first_time/last_time/before/after predicates to produce the final evidence set R' (p. 4, Section 3.3) — a stated fusion of similarity ranking and structured filtering.

Evaluation is confined to the public EgoLifeQA benchmark (500-question subset for participant Jake) against a reproduced EgoRAG baseline under a controlled LLM setup, run on a single NVIDIA L40 GPU (p. 5). No deployed system, real users, or field setting appears in the given pages.

EgoRAG is deliberately reproduced with the same LLM (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) and captioner 'to isolate the contribution of memory representation from LLM capacity... ensuring that performance differences arise from memory representation and retrieval design' (p. 5) — a manipulated-condition-vs-control design, further corroborated by systematic component-removal ablations (Table 5, stage-wise removal of Event-Prototype Assignment / Interaction Importance / Interaction Consolidation, and Table 8, zeroing each Eq. 3 term, both p. 15).

Self-described throughout as an architecture rather than a single technique: abstract calls it 'an interaction-centric memory framework' (p. 1), and the contributions list on p. 2 introduces 'Imprint, a cognitively inspired online memory compression framework' spanning pattern discovery, importance estimation, and consolidation stages.
